- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +10% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.4) and price drops, model underreacts; add 1–3% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >85 and true is <75, adjust downward by 5–10% for next period.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8), model overfits short-term noise; use 5-day rolling average to filter out sentiment-driven spikes.
- For horizon >15d, model tends to underestimate downward trends; add 1–3% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
